First, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{OA}=a=3i-2j-k, \\  & \overset{\to }{OB}=b=3i-2j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the coordinates of $-2a+b$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-2a+b & =-2(3i-2j-k)+(3i-2j) \\  & =-6i+4j+2k+3i-2j \\  & =-3i+2j+2k.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector, we need to divide the vector by its length:

$$
u=\frac{-2a+b}{|\,-2a+b\,|}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|u| & =\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+4+4} \\  & =\sqrt{17}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we divide the vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}\cdot ⟨-3,2,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{3}{\sqrt{17}},\,\frac{2}{\sqrt{17}},\,\frac{2}{\sqrt{17}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
